questions.q: What is the authoritative documentation source for T-SQL, per this lesson?
options: learn.microsoft.com
docs.oracle.com
dev.mysql.com/doc/refman
postgresql.org/docs
questions.explain: learn.microsoft.com is Microsoft's official SQL Server/T-SQL reference, versioned by SQL Server release and by Azure SQL.

questions.q: What does this lesson specifically call out about PostgreSQL's official documentation?
options: It is widely regarded as some of the best technical documentation in the open-source world, with thorough worked examples
It is the least detailed of the five references in this lesson
It has no version-specific pages at all
It only covers PL/pgSQL, not plain SQL
questions.explain: postgresql.org/docs is called out directly as genuinely thorough and well-organized, worth checking even when you're unsure PostgreSQL has the answer.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the single most important habit when consulting any dialect's documentation?
options: Confirming the doc page's version matches the actual version/edition you're running against
Always reading the documentation in alphabetical order by platform
Only trusting documentation that has no code examples
Avoiding vendor documentation entirely in favor of forums
questions.explain: Every platform in this course has changed behavior across versions -- MySQL 8.0's CTE support being the clearest example -- so matching the doc version to the actual running version is the key habit.

questions.q: Which real example from this course illustrates why checking the MySQL version against the docs matters?
options: MySQL only gained CTE and window function support starting in version 8.0
MySQL has never changed any behavior across versions
MySQL's documentation has no version selector
CTEs have always worked identically on every MySQL version
questions.explain: The capstone lesson's MySQL translation depended specifically on MySQL 8.0+ for its CTE and window function syntax -- a clear real-world version gate.

questions.q: Where should you look for documentation on cloud warehouse platforms like Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, and Redshift?
options: Each vendor's own official documentation site
Only in Oracle's documentation, since it covers all SQL dialects
There is no documentation available for cloud warehouse platforms
Only in third-party blog posts, never vendor docs
questions.explain: Each cloud warehouse vendor maintains its own official docs -- docs.snowflake.com, docs.databricks.com, cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs, and docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift.
